topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: CPU-Storage
explanation: A memory hierarchy mitigates the CPU-storage latency gap by structuring storage into tiered levels (registers, L1/L2/L3 caches, main memory, secondary storage), prioritizing speed and proximity to the processor. Caching is the core strategy within this hierarchy, exploiting the principle of locality of reference. This principle includes temporal locality (re-accessing recent data) and spatial locality (accessing nearby data). Data is transferred between levels in fixed-size units called cache lines. System performance is directly tied to the cache hit rate; a cache miss necessitates a costly fetch from a lower level, resulting in a pipeline stall. Effective cache management minimizes memory access latency and maximizes instruction throughput.
